## Background

There are many *graphics systems* in R for making plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**.

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems:

We can use the in-built `cars` dataset:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

A base R plot:

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**.

Before I can use ggplot2 I need to install it on my computer. To do this we can use the function `install.packages("ggplot2")`
 
> **N.B.** We never run an `install.packages()` in our quarto doc (we run it in our R console) as it would re-install the package every time I render my document.

Once installed we still need to load up the package into our R session. We do this with a `library()` call

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs:

- the **data** (a data.frame of the stuff we want to plot)
- the **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot),
- the **geom** layer (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point()
```

## Lets add some features (more layers)

Let's add a trend line that shows the relationship between `speed` and `distance`:

```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() 
```

```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
```

 Add a theme, custom axis labels and plot title:
 
```{r}
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Speed (MPH", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Stopping distance of some old cars")
```
 
## Gene Expression Plot

First we will read some expression data for the effects of a GLP-1 drug

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("blue","gray","red") ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="No drug", 
       y="Drug",
       title="GLP-1 Inhibitor Effects on Gene Expression")
```

> Q. Use the nrow() function to find out how many genes are in this dataset. What is your answer?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. Use the table() function on the State column of this data.frame to find out how many ‘up’ regulated genes there are. What is your answer?

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

> Q. Using your values above and 2 significant figures. What fraction of total genes is up-regulated in this dataset?

```{r}
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.up    <- sum( genes$State == "up" )

round( (n.up/n.total*100), 2)
```

## Going Further

Here we read the famous *gapmider* dataset:

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many different "country" values are in this dataset?

```{r}
length( table(gapminder$country) )
```

```{r}
length( unique(gapminder$country) )
```
Let's make our first plot of `gdpPercap` vs `lifeExp`:

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.2)
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point()

```

One useful layer we can add to explore big datasets like this is called "facetting"

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~continent)

```

### Limit to 1977 and 2007 

We can install and use the **dplyr** package to help us "filter" the full dataset down to a smaller subset that only includes the years we want.

First wee need to run `install.packages("dplyr")` and then load it with `library(dplyr)`.


```{r}
library(dplyr)

filter(gapminder, year==2007, country=="Ireland")
filter(gapminder, year==1977, country=="Ireland")

#gapminder$year
```

> Q. Make a histogram of lifeExp fill color by continent

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
